term.name: Transposition cipher
term.short: A transposition cipher encrypts by rearranging plaintext symbols according to a key without replacing them.
term.meta_title: Transposition Cipher — Definition and Examples | CiphersOnline
term.meta_description: Learn how transposition ciphers reorder text, how rail fence and columnar methods work, and how transposition differs from substitution.

body.title: Definition
body.html: A transposition cipher changes the positions of plaintext symbols according to a reversible permutation. The symbols themselves remain unchanged, so the ciphertext usually has exactly the same letter counts as the plaintext.

body.title: How it works
body.html: Rail fence writes text along rows and reads it in another order. Columnar transposition writes text into a grid and reads columns in an order set by a keyword or numerical key. Decryption reconstructs the layout and applies the inverse permutation.

body.title: Cryptanalysis
body.html: Single transpositions preserve letter frequencies and can expose characteristic fragments when candidate layouts are tested. Repeated or combined transpositions are harder, but classical forms do not provide modern security.

faq.question: Does transposition change the letters?
faq.answer: No. It changes their positions; padding symbols may be added only to fill a layout.

faq.question: How does it differ from substitution?
faq.answer: Transposition reorders existing symbols, while substitution replaces symbols and normally preserves their positions.
